advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove `cross_session_warning` from `GateResultOut._omit_when_unset` (it is always explicitly set, so the entry is dead) or clarify the comment that it is null-tolerant unlike the integer metrics.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_models.py:64-68: `_drop_unset_nullless_fields` only pops a field when `name not in self.model_fields_set`
src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:512: result["cross_session_warning"] = _cross_session(ticket_id)  (always sets the key -> always in model_fields_set)

TicketStateOut (line 154) and WriteAckOut (line 314) declare cross_session_warning but do NOT list it in _omit_when_unset, emitting null when silent — GateResultOut's extra entry has no effect on wire bytes.
advisory.finding: `cross_session_warning` is listed in `GateResultOut._omit_when_unset`, but both `check_ac` and `quality_check` always assign the key explicitly (`result["cross_session_warning"] = _cross_session(ticket_id)`), so the field is always in `model_fields_set` and the omit-when-unset branch never fires for it. The entry is dead code, and it sits under a comment that describes integer metrics which 'must stay ABSENT rather than become null' — misleading, since this string field is always set and (correctly) serialized as null when silent, matching TicketStateOut/WriteAckOut.
scenarios: A future reader assumes cross_session_warning is omitted-when-unset on the gate surface and relies on absence, but the wire always carries an explicit null when there is no warning.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop "cross_session_warning" from the `_omit_when_unset` tuple in GateResultOut so it matches TicketStateOut/WriteAckOut, which declare the field without omitting it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend test_same_session_is_silent (or add a case) to assert check_ac, quality_check, and declare_no_file_impact return cross_session_warning is None when the holder runs them.
evidence: test_same_session_is_silent asserts only: `assert _read_tools()["show_ticket"](tid).cross_session_warning is None` and `assert _write_tools()["comment_ticket"](tid, "mine").cross_session_warning is None` (lines 197-198)

Named violating input: holder sess-A running `check_ac(tid)` / `quality_check(tid)` / `declare_no_file_impact(tid, reason)` on its own claimed ticket should yield cross_session_warning is None, but no test covers that silent path for the newly added lines in _mcp_reads.py:512,520 and _mcp_writes.py declare_no_file_impact.
The positive-warning tests (test_gate_reads_warn_for_other_session, test_declare_no_file_impact_warns_and_still_mutates) only cover the other-session case.
advisory.finding: The same-session negative control does not exercise the newly added surfaces: it asserts cross_session_warning is None only for show_ticket and comment_ticket, not for the diff's new check_ac/quality_check reads or declare_no_file_impact. A regression that made these emit the advisory to the holder itself would go undetected.
scenarios: A change to _cross_session or the gate wiring that leaks the advisory to the holder itself would pass CI.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the MCP `declare_no_file_impact` output change from unstructured string `"ok"` to structured `WriteAckOut` is an intended, acceptable wire-contract change for external MCP clients (no compatibility shim / versioning needed).
evidence: Diff: `-    @mcp.tool(annotations=_ANN["MUTATE_IDEMPOTENT"], structured_output=False)` / `-    def declare_no_file_impact(ticket_id: str, reason: str) -> str:` changed to `+    @mcp.tool(annotations=_ANN["MUTATE_IDEMPOTENT"])` / `+    def declare_no_file_impact(ticket_id: str, reason: str) -> WriteAckOut:`

src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:485 `def declare_no_file_impact(ticket_id: str, reason: str) -> WriteAckOut:` returning `_ack(...)` which is `WriteAckOut.model_validate({"result": ..., "push_status": ..., "description_warning": ..., "cross_session_warning": ...})` (src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:98-105)

Prior contract evidence: the pre-change test asserted the raw string form `-    assert result == "ok"` and `-    assert not tools["declare_no_file_impact"].outputSchema` at tests/interfaces/facades/test_file_impact_scope_heldout.py, now rewritten to `result["result"] == "ok"` — confirming the observable output shape changed from string to object.

Public surface: `declare_no_file_impact` is exported and documented as an MCP tool (docs/mcp-reference.md:81) and registered via `@mcp.tool`; external MCP clients are off-repo and cannot be greped, so no repo callsite disproves external breakage.
blocking.finding: The public MCP tool `declare_no_file_impact` changes its output contract from an unstructured string `"ok"` (previously `structured_output=False`, return type `str`) to a structured `WriteAckOut` object `{result, push_status, description_warning, cross_session_warning}`. This is an unversioned wire-shape change on an external tool surface: MCP clients that consumed the result as the bare text `"ok"` (the prior contract) now receive a structured object instead of a string.
scenarios: An external MCP client/agent that called declare_no_file_impact and compared the returned text content to "ok" (matching the previous unstructured-string contract) now receives a JSON object and its equality/parse breaks.
Any MCP client relying on declare_no_file_impact advertising NO outputSchema now sees an outputSchema and structured content.
